## TL;DR

The 401 came from UI handoff verification capturing the regular `/secrets` route without an authenticated session. That route correctly requests `/api/project-environments`, and the server correctly returns 401 when the caller is not signed in. The verification shot had no fixture, even though the page already has a registered `secrets:populated` fixture that renders fake environment data locally and avoids the protected request. I declared the Secrets handoff shot with that fixture, added a regression assertion that the capture URL state is recognized by the UI fixture reader, and updated the November QA note to distinguish the automated shot fix from outstanding authenticated QA.

## Work and rationale

I read the task specification and the relevant QA record, then followed the code path from `SecretsView.vue` to its `loadEnvironments` request and fixture setup. The page is designed to call the environment API in normal operation. It must not make that API public or weaken the server’s authentication guard just to make unauthenticated screenshots look clean. The existing fixture branch already initializes a fake `dev-nick` environment, creates a local key inventory, and skips `loadEnvironments`; it is the correct rendering mode for a no-auth handoff shot.

The reported behavior was therefore a mismatch between the shot plan and the preview’s auth context, not an endpoint authorization bug. I added a declared `/secrets` shot using `state: "secrets:populated"`, with a label and a highlight target on the rendered inventory. I also extended the shot-fixture test so it verifies that the URL builder encodes the state and that the UI-side reader recognizes the resulting query parameter as `secrets:populated`. That assertion guards the link between the handoff capture plan and the fixture dispatch mechanism.

I updated `docs/qa/2026-11-web-qa-pass.md` to record that handoff verification now uses local fixture data and avoids the protected request. The record explicitly preserves the limit of the original visual QA: no signed-in Secrets behavior was observed. It also lists the remaining #1157 follow-ups: #1163 for the incomplete Checks tab interaction pass, #1164 for authenticated Secrets behavior, and #1165 for Agents authentication guidance with a suitable test setup.

## Approaches tried

I considered treating the 401 as expected in verification, but the shot system already supports seeded page state and the Secrets component already has a suitable fixture. Using that fixture avoids generating the console error and displays a useful, deterministic page state without adding an exception to the UI verification gate.

I also traced whether the fixture state might still trigger the real environment fetch. `SecretsView.vue` sets the fake environment and calls its fixture-aware `loadSnapshot` branch on mount; it only calls `loadEnvironments` in the non-fixture branch. The capture URL test now verifies that the declared state is correctly read by the UI. This test covers the wiring that makes the shot bypass the live fetch.

## Challenges and blockers

The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` first failed its formatter step on the new test. I ran `bun run fmt` and reran the check. The successful run passed formatting, lint, the build, CSS and theme guards, rendered contrast, bare-require and artifact checks, remote validation, and the UI smoke test. The remote changed-path test run reported 105 tests passed. RepoOS temporarily held local work at its pressure guard; I waited until it proceeded.

This session did not run a browser shot capture itself. RepoOS owns managed preview capture, and the task instructions say the declared shots are captured at handoff. The handoff plan now targets the fixture state, but the resulting screenshot and any per-shot capture verdict will be produced by RepoOS after this turn. The authenticated Secrets flow remains unverified and is still tracked by #1164.

## Key learnings

A protected endpoint’s expected 401 can still be a real verification defect when an automated shot uses the live page route without the page’s registered preview fixture. For no-auth captures, seed representative UI data locally and leave server authorization intact. A route plus fixture state must both be declared in the shot plan, and the fixture state should be recognized by the UI before capture. Finally, recording an automated screenshot fix does not establish authenticated product behavior; QA notes should state that boundary and keep the corresponding human or environment-dependent follow-up open.
